# InterImm Mars Clock: full reference for language models

Everything needed to answer questions about time on Mars, or to compute it without any tool.
Source: https://github.com/InterImm/mars-clock (MIT). Short version: https://interimm.org/mars-clock/llms.txt

## Computing Mars time by hand (Mars24, NASA GISS)

Input: an Earth instant in UTC. Angles in degrees.

1. millis = milliseconds since 1970-01-01T00:00:00Z
2. JD_UT = 2440587.5 + millis / 86400000
3. TAI−UTC: 37 s since 2017-01-01 (36 s from 2015-07-01, 35 s from 2012-07-01, 34 s from 2009-01-01, 33 s from 2006-01-01, 32 s from 1999-01-01)
4. JD_TT = JD_UT + (TAI−UTC + 32.184) / 86400
5. Δt = JD_TT − 2451545.0   (days since J2000)
6. M = 19.3871 + 0.52402073 × Δt   (Mars mean anomaly, mod 360)
7. α_FMS = 270.3871 + 0.524038496 × Δt   (mod 360)
8. PBS = Σ A_i cos(0.985626 × Δt / τ_i + φ_i) with (A, τ, φ) =
   (0.0071, 2.2353, 49.409), (0.0057, 2.7543, 168.173), (0.0039, 1.1177, 191.837), (0.0037, 15.7866, 21.736),
   (0.0021, 2.1354, 15.704), (0.0020, 2.4694, 95.528), (0.0018, 32.8493, 49.095)
9. ν − M = (10.691 + 3.0e−7 Δt) sin M + 0.623 sin 2M + 0.050 sin 3M + 0.005 sin 4M + 0.0005 sin 5M + PBS
10. Ls = α_FMS + (ν − M)   (mod 360; 0 = northern spring equinox, 90 = northern summer solstice, 180 = autumn equinox, 270 = winter solstice)
11. EOT = 2.861 sin 2Ls − 0.071 sin 4Ls + 0.002 sin 6Ls − (ν − M)   degrees; hours = EOT / 15
12. MSD = (Δt − 4.5) / 1.0274912517 + 44796.0 − 0.0009626   (Mars Sol Date)
13. MTC = (24 × MSD) mod 24   (Coordinated Mars Time, hours)
14. LMST at longitude λ (degrees east) = MTC + λ / 15   (mod 24)
15. LTST = LMST + EOT / 15   (mod 24)
16. Solar declination = asin(0.42565 sin Ls) + 0.25 sin Ls
17. Sun distance (AU) = 1.5236 (1.00436 − 0.09309 cos M − 0.004336 cos 2M − 0.00031 cos 3M − 0.00003 cos 4M)

Check: 2000-01-06T00:00:00Z gives Ls = 277.1876, MSD = 44795.9998, MTC = 23:59:39.

Mission sols count local mean solar days at the landing site, sol 0 = landing sol:
sol = floor(MSD + λ/360) − floor(MSD_landing + λ/360).
Curiosity landed 2012-08-06T05:17:57Z at 137.4417°E. Perseverance landed 2021-02-18T20:55:00Z at 77.4509°E.

Mars Year (Clancy et al. 2000): MY 1 began 1955-04-11 (Ls = 0). A Mars year is 668.5921 sols (686.97 Earth days).
Recent starts: MY 36 2021-02-07, MY 37 2022-12-26, MY 38 2024-11-12, MY 39 2026-09-30, MY 40 2028-08-17.

## InterImm calendar and clock

- Sol count: S = MSD − 34242.0288 (InterImm epoch, exact constant 34242.2718 + 0.73027 − 1/1.0274912517). Year 1 day 1 began at S = 0 (1970-04-28 UTC).
- Year Y has 668 sols, or 669 when Y + 1 is "leap": n is leap if n is odd or divisible by 10, except multiples of 100 are not, multiples of 1000 are, multiples of 3000 are not.
- 24 months: months 6, 12, 18, 24 have 27 sols, others 28; in a 669-sol year month 24 has 28. Every month starts on a Sunday (7-sol weeks restart each month).
- Month names (solar terms): 1 春分 Chunfen, 2 清明 Qingming, 3 谷雨 Guyu, 4 立夏 Lixia, 5 小满 Xiaoman, 6 芒种 Mangzhong, 7 夏至 Xiazhi, 8 小暑 Xiaoshu, 9 大暑 Dashu, 10 立秋 Liqiu, 11 处暑 Chushu, 12 白露 Bailu, 13 秋分 Qiufen, 14 寒露 Hanlu, 15 霜降 Shuangjiang, 16 立冬 Lidong, 17 小雪 Xiaoxue, 18 大雪 Daxue, 19 冬至 Dongzhi, 20 小寒 Xiaohan, 21 大寒 Dahan, 22 立春 Lichun, 23 雨水 Yushui, 24 惊蛰 Jingzhe.
- Clock: Earth-length hours. hours = frac(S + offset/24.6598) × 24.6598, shown as hh:mm:ss below 24 h and +mm:ss after (up to +39:35).
- Timezones 0-24, each 14.5987° wide eastward from Airy-0; zone k is k hours ahead of zone 0, except zone 24 which is 39 min 35 s behind (24 h ahead modulo the 24.6598 h sol).

## The library source (lib/marstime.js)

```js
// marstime.js: Martian time from Earth time, in plain JavaScript with no dependencies.
//
// Implements the Mars24 algorithm (Allison & McEwen 2000, NASA GISS: https://www.giss.nasa.gov/tools/mars24/help/algorithm.html)
// plus the InterImm calendar, clock and timezones that the InterImm Mars clock has shown since 2016.
// Works in browsers, Node, Deno and Bun. Every function is pure: pass a Date (or ms since 1970) and get numbers back.
//
//   import { marsTime } from 'https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/InterImm/mars-clock@gh-pages/lib/marstime.js';
//   marsTime(new Date()).mtc   // Coordinated Mars Time, hours
//
// Released under the MIT licence (see LICENSE). Based on jtauber's mars-clock (MIT).

export const VERSION = '1.0.0';

const DAY_MS = 86400000;
/** Length of a Mars solar day (sol) in Earth days. */
export const SOL_IN_DAYS = 1.0274912517;
/** Length of a sol in SI seconds (88775.244 s = 24 h 39 min 35.244 s). */
export const SOL_IN_SECONDS = SOL_IN_DAYS * 86400;
/** Mean length of a Mars tropical year (vernal equinox to vernal equinox), in sols. */
export const YEAR_IN_SOLS = 668.5921;

const rad = (d) => (d * Math.PI) / 180;
const sin = (d) => Math.sin(rad(d));
const cos = (d) => Math.cos(rad(d));
const mod = (x, n) => ((x % n) + n) % n;
const toMs = (date) => {
  const ms = typeof date === 'number' ? date : +date;
  if (!Number.isFinite(ms)) throw new TypeError('marstime: expected a valid Date or a number of milliseconds');
  return ms;
};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- Earth time scales

/**
 * Leap seconds: [first UTC day, TAI-UTC in seconds], from the IERS list
 * (https://hpiers.obspm.fr/iers/bul/bulc/Leap_Second.dat). No leap second has been added since 2017-01-01.
 * When IERS announces a new one, append a row here; the tests check the table stays sorted.
 */
export const LEAP_SECONDS = [
  ['1972-01-01', 10], ['1972-07-01', 11], ['1973-01-01', 12], ['1974-01-01', 13], ['1975-01-01', 14],
  ['1976-01-01', 15], ['1977-01-01', 16], ['1978-01-01', 17], ['1979-01-01', 18], ['1980-01-01', 19],
  ['1981-07-01', 20], ['1982-07-01', 21], ['1983-07-01', 22], ['1985-07-01', 23], ['1988-01-01', 24],
  ['1990-01-01', 25], ['1991-01-01', 26], ['1992-07-01', 27], ['1993-07-01', 28], ['1994-07-01', 29],
  ['1996-01-01', 30], ['1997-07-01', 31], ['1999-01-01', 32], ['2006-01-01', 33], ['2009-01-01', 34],
  ['2012-07-01', 35], ['2015-07-01', 36], ['2017-01-01', 37],
];
const LEAP_MS = LEAP_SECONDS.map(([d, s]) => [Date.parse(d + 'T00:00:00Z'), s]);

/** TAI-UTC in seconds at a UTC instant. Before 1972 UTC was not whole-second based; 10 s is used there. */
export function taiMinusUtc(date) {
  const ms = toMs(date);
  let s = 10;
  for (const [t, v] of LEAP_MS) {
    if (ms >= t) s = v;
    else break;
  }
  return s;
}

/** Julian dates for an instant: jdUt (UTC), jdTt (Terrestrial Time) and days since J2000.0 (TT). */
export function julianDates(date) {
  const ms = toMs(date);
  const jdUt = 2440587.5 + ms / DAY_MS;
  const jdTt = jdUt + (taiMinusUtc(ms) + 32.184) / 86400;
  return { jdUt, jdTt, j2000: jdTt - 2451545.0 };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- Mars24

/** Mars Sol Date: sols since 1873-12-29 (the Mars24 epoch), as a decimal. */
export function marsSolDate(date) {
  return (julianDates(date).j2000 - 4.5) / SOL_IN_DAYS + 44796.0 - 0.0009626;
}

/** The Earth instant (a Date) for a Mars Sol Date. Inverse of marsSolDate, accurate to well under a millisecond. */
export function dateFromMarsSolDate(msd) {
  const jdTt = (msd - 44796.0 + 0.0009626) * SOL_IN_DAYS + 4.5 + 2451545.0;
  // TT -> UTC needs TAI-UTC at the answer; two passes settle it (the first guess is within a minute).
  let ms = (jdTt - 2440587.5) * DAY_MS - (37 + 32.184) * 1000;
  for (let i = 0; i < 2; i++) ms = (jdTt - 2440587.5) * DAY_MS - (taiMinusUtc(ms) + 32.184) * 1000;
  return new Date(Math.ceil(ms)); // round up so the answer never falls just before the requested moment
}

// Ls at which each Clancy Mars Year starts is 0. Mars Year 1 began on 1955-04-11 (Clancy et al. 2000).
// This is the Mars Sol Date of that equinox, found with marsTime() itself and pinned by the tests.
export const MY1_START_MSD = 28892.66;

/**
 * Everything Mars24 gives for one instant, optionally at a longitude on Mars.
 * @param {Date|number} date  the Earth instant
 * @param {object} [opts]
 * @param {number} [opts.longitude=0]  degrees EAST of the prime meridian (Airy-0). West longitudes are negative.
 * @returns {{
 *   msd: number, mtc: number, ls: number, marsYear: number, eot: number,
 *   lmst: number, ltst: number, subsolarLongitude: number, solarDeclination: number,
 *   heliocentricDistance: number, meanAnomaly: number, sol: number
 * }}
 *   msd: Mars Sol Date; mtc: Coordinated Mars Time (hours, 0-24, Mars hours of sol/24);
 *   ls: areocentric solar longitude, the season (degrees, 0 = northern spring equinox);
 *   marsYear: Clancy Mars Year number; eot: equation of time (Mars hours);
 *   lmst / ltst: local mean / true solar time at the longitude (Mars hours);
 *   subsolarLongitude: degrees east; solarDeclination: degrees; heliocentricDistance: AU;
 *   sol: whole Mars Sol Date at the longitude (local sol count since the MSD epoch).
 */
export function marsTime(date, { longitude = 0 } = {}) {
  const ms = toMs(date);
  const { j2000 } = julianDates(ms);
  const M = mod(19.3871 + 0.52402073 * j2000, 360);
  const alphaFms = mod(270.3871 + 0.524038496 * j2000, 360);
  const pbs = [
    [0.0071, 2.2353, 49.409], [0.0057, 2.7543, 168.173], [0.0039, 1.1177, 191.837], [0.0037, 15.7866, 21.736],
    [0.0021, 2.1354, 15.704], [0.002, 2.4694, 95.528], [0.0018, 32.8493, 49.095],
  ].reduce((s, [a, tau, phi]) => s + a * cos((0.985626 * j2000) / tau + phi), 0);
  const nu = (10.691 + 3.0e-7 * j2000) * sin(M) + 0.623 * sin(2 * M) + 0.05 * sin(3 * M) + 0.005 * sin(4 * M) +
    0.0005 * sin(5 * M) + pbs; // equation of centre, degrees
  const ls = mod(alphaFms + nu, 360);
  const eotDeg = 2.861 * sin(2 * ls) - 0.071 * sin(4 * ls) + 0.002 * sin(6 * ls) - nu;
  const eot = (eotDeg * 24) / 360;
  const msd = (j2000 - 4.5) / SOL_IN_DAYS + 44796.0 - 0.0009626;
  const mtc = mod(24 * msd, 24);
  const lmst = mod(mtc + longitude / 15, 24);
  const ltst = mod(lmst + eot, 24);
  const subsolarLongitude = mod(-(mtc * 15 + eotDeg + 180), 360);
  const solarDeclination = Math.asin(0.42565 * sin(ls)) * (180 / Math.PI) + 0.25 * sin(ls);
  const heliocentricDistance = 1.5236 * (1.00436 - 0.09309 * cos(M) - 0.004336 * cos(2 * M) - 0.00031 * cos(3 * M) -
    0.00003 * cos(4 * M));
  // Mars Year: count mean years since MY 1 began. Ls never strays more than ~25 degrees from the mean phase,
  // so a large gap between the two means the equinox has (or hasn't yet) passed.
  const years = (msd - MY1_START_MSD) / YEAR_IN_SOLS;
  let marsYear = Math.floor(years) + 1;
  const gap = ls - (years - Math.floor(years)) * 360;
  if (gap < -180) marsYear += 1;
  else if (gap > 180) marsYear -= 1;
  return {
    msd, mtc, ls, marsYear, eot, lmst, ltst, subsolarLongitude, solarDeclination, heliocentricDistance,
    meanAnomaly: M, sol: Math.floor(msd + longitude / 360),
  };
}

/** Season names for an Ls, per hemisphere. */
export function season(ls) {
  const names = ['spring', 'summer', 'autumn', 'winter'];
  const q = Math.floor(mod(ls, 360) / 90);
  return { north: names[q], south: names[(q + 2) % 4] };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- Missions

/**
 * Landers and rovers that count their own sols. Sol 0 is the landing sol, counted in local mean solar time at the site.
 * longitude is degrees east. `active` reflects public mission status when this table was last edited.
 */
export const MISSIONS = {
  curiosity: { name: 'Curiosity', landed: '2012-08-06T05:17:57Z', longitude: 137.4417, active: true },
  perseverance: { name: 'Perseverance', landed: '2021-02-18T20:55:00Z', longitude: 77.4509, active: true },
  zhurong: { name: 'Zhurong', landed: '2021-05-14T23:18:00Z', longitude: 109.925, active: false },
  insight: { name: 'InSight', landed: '2018-11-26T19:52:59Z', longitude: 135.6234, active: false },
  opportunity: { name: 'Opportunity', landed: '2004-01-25T05:05:00Z', longitude: 354.4734, active: false },
  spirit: { name: 'Spirit', landed: '2004-01-04T04:35:00Z', longitude: 175.4729, active: false },
};

/**
 * A mission's sol number and local times. `mission` is a key of MISSIONS or an object { landed, longitude }.
 * Note: Spirit and Opportunity used their own Earth-day-aligned mission clocks; this gives the LMST-based count.
 */
export function missionTime(date, mission) {
  const m = typeof mission === 'string' ? MISSIONS[mission] : mission;
  if (!m) throw new Error(`marstime: unknown mission ${mission}`);
  const here = marsTime(date, { longitude: m.longitude });
  const landing = marsTime(Date.parse(m.landed), { longitude: m.longitude });
  return { sol: here.sol - landing.sol, lmst: here.lmst, ltst: here.ltst };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- InterImm calendar, clock and timezones
//
// The InterImm calendar (https://interimm.org/mars-clock/en/cal-doc.html): 24 months in 4 seasons of 6, named after
// the Chinese solar terms; months 6, 12, 18 and 24 have 27 sols, the rest 28; a leap year adds a sol to month 24.
// Year 1 began at the northern spring equinox of 1970-04-28.
// The InterImm clock counts Earth-length hours: a sol runs 00:00:00 to 23:59:59, then +00:00 to +39:35.
// The 25 timezones are each one Earth hour (14.5987 degrees) wide, eastward from Airy-0.

// Offset (sols) between Mars Sol Date and the InterImm day count; kept exactly as in the original clock.
const INTERIMM_EPOCH_MSD = 34242.2718 + 0.73027 - 1 / SOL_IN_DAYS;
const HOURS_PER_SOL = 24 * SOL_IN_DAYS; // 24.6598 Earth hours

/** Leap rule of the InterImm calendar applied to a number. */
export function interimmLeapRule(n) {
  if (n % 3000 === 0) return false;
  if (n % 1000 === 0) return true;
  if (n % 100 === 0) return false;
  return n % 2 !== 0 || n % 10 === 0;
}

/**
 * Whether InterImm year `year` has 669 sols. The original clock applied the leap rule to year + 1, and every date it
 * has shown follows that, so it is kept here (see README, "InterImm calendar").
 */
export function isInterimmLeapYear(year) {
  return interimmLeapRule(year + 1);
}

/** Sols in an InterImm year. */
export const interimmYearLength = (year) => 668 + (isInterimmLeapYear(year) ? 1 : 0);

/** Sols in an InterImm month (1-24). */
export function interimmMonthLength(year, month) {
  if (month === 24) return 27 + (isInterimmLeapYear(year) ? 1 : 0);
  return month % 6 === 0 ? 27 : 28;
}

/** Month names: the 24 solar terms, starting from the spring equinox. */
export const INTERIMM_MONTHS = [
  ['春分', 'Chunfen'], ['清明', 'Qingming'], ['谷雨', 'Guyu'], ['立夏', 'Lixia'], ['小满', 'Xiaoman'], ['芒种', 'Mangzhong'],
  ['夏至', 'Xiazhi'], ['小暑', 'Xiaoshu'], ['大暑', 'Dashu'], ['立秋', 'Liqiu'], ['处暑', 'Chushu'], ['白露', 'Bailu'],
  ['秋分', 'Qiufen'], ['寒露', 'Hanlu'], ['霜降', 'Shuangjiang'], ['立冬', 'Lidong'], ['小雪', 'Xiaoxue'], ['大雪', 'Daxue'],
  ['冬至', 'Dongzhi'], ['小寒', 'Xiaohan'], ['大寒', 'Dahan'], ['立春', 'Lichun'], ['雨水', 'Yushui'], ['惊蛰', 'Jingzhe'],
].map(([zh, en], i) => ({ month: i + 1, zh, en }));

const WEEKDAYS = ['Sunday', 'Monday', 'Tuesday', 'Wednesday', 'Thursday', 'Friday', 'Saturday'];

/** Width of one InterImm timezone in degrees of longitude. */
export const INTERIMM_ZONE_WIDTH = 360 / HOURS_PER_SOL; // 14.5987

/** InterImm timezone (0-24) for a longitude in degrees east. */
export function interimmZone(longitude) {
  return Math.min(24, Math.floor(mod(longitude, 360) / INTERIMM_ZONE_WIDTH));
}

/** Offset of an InterImm timezone from zone 0, in Earth hours. Zone 24 is 24 h ahead, i.e. 39:35 behind zone 0. */
export function interimmZoneOffset(zone) {
  if (!Number.isInteger(zone) || zone < 0 || zone > 24) throw new RangeError('marstime: InterImm zones are 0-24');
  return zone === 24 ? 24 - HOURS_PER_SOL : zone;
}

/** Break an InterImm sol count into year, month, day. `days` counts sols since the start of Year 1. */
function interimmCalendar(days) {
  let year = 1;
  let d = Math.floor(days);
  while (d < 0) { year -= 1; d += interimmYearLength(year); }
  while (d >= interimmYearLength(year)) { d -= interimmYearLength(year); year += 1; }
  const dayOfYear = d + 1;
  let month = 1;
  while (month < 24 && d >= interimmMonthLength(year, month)) { d -= interimmMonthLength(year, month); month += 1; }
  return { year, month, day: d + 1, dayOfYear };
}

/**
 * Format Earth hours into the InterImm clock reading: "hh:mm:ss" for the first 24 hours of the sol,
 * "+mm:ss" for the 39 min 35 s after that.
 */
export function formatInterimmClock(hours) {
  const total = Math.floor(hours * 3600 + 1e-6);
  if (total < 86400) {
    const p = (n) => String(n).padStart(2, '0');
    return `${p(Math.floor(total / 3600))}:${p(Math.floor(total / 60) % 60)}:${p(total % 60)}`;
  }
  const extra = total - 86400;
  return `+${String(Math.floor(extra / 60)).padStart(2, '0')}:${String(extra % 60).padStart(2, '0')}`;
}

/**
 * InterImm date and clock time at an instant, in an InterImm timezone (0-24).
 * @returns {{year:number, month:number, day:number, dayOfYear:number, weekday:string, monthName:{zh:string,en:string},
 *   hours:number, clock:string, zone:number, solCount:number, leapYear:boolean}}
 *   hours: Earth hours since the start of the sol (0 to 24.6598); clock: formatted reading;
 *   solCount: sols since the start of Year 1 in that zone, as a decimal.
 */
export function interimmTime(date, { zone = 0 } = {}) {
  const msd = marsSolDate(date);
  const solCount = msd - INTERIMM_EPOCH_MSD + interimmZoneOffset(zone) / HOURS_PER_SOL;
  const cal = interimmCalendar(solCount);
  const hours = mod(solCount, 1) * HOURS_PER_SOL;
  const { zh, en } = INTERIMM_MONTHS[cal.month - 1];
  return {
    ...cal, weekday: WEEKDAYS[(cal.day - 1) % 7], monthName: { zh, en }, hours, clock: formatInterimmClock(hours),
    zone, solCount, leapYear: isInterimmLeapYear(cal.year),
  };
}

/** The Earth instant (Date) at which an InterImm date and clock time occur. Inverse of interimmTime. */
export function dateFromInterimm({ year, month = 1, day = 1, hours = 0, zone = 0 }) {
  if (month < 1 || month > 24) throw new RangeError('marstime: month must be 1-24');
  if (day < 1 || day > interimmMonthLength(year, month)) throw new RangeError('marstime: day out of range for month');
  if (hours < 0 || hours >= HOURS_PER_SOL) throw new RangeError('marstime: hours must be 0 to 24.6598');
  let sols = 0;
  for (let y = 1; y < year; y++) sols += interimmYearLength(y);
  for (let y = year; y < 1; y++) sols -= interimmYearLength(y);
  for (let m = 1; m < month; m++) sols += interimmMonthLength(year, m);
  sols += day - 1 + hours / HOURS_PER_SOL;
  return dateFromMarsSolDate(sols + INTERIMM_EPOCH_MSD - interimmZoneOffset(zone) / HOURS_PER_SOL);
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- formatting

/** Format hours as "hh:mm:ss" (wraps into 0-24; negative values get a leading minus). */
export function formatHms(hours) {
  const sign = hours < 0 ? '-' : '';
  const total = Math.floor(Math.abs(hours) * 3600 + 1e-6);
  const p = (n) => String(n).padStart(2, '0');
  return `${sign}${p(Math.floor(total / 3600))}:${p(Math.floor(total / 60) % 60)}:${p(total % 60)}`;
}

/** One object with everything, handy for JSON output. */
export function snapshot(date = Date.now(), { longitude = 0, zone = 0 } = {}) {
  const ms = toMs(date);
  const t = marsTime(ms, { longitude });
  const i = interimmTime(ms, { zone });
  const missions = Object.fromEntries(
    Object.entries(MISSIONS).filter(([, m]) => m.active && Date.parse(m.landed) <= ms)
      .map(([k]) => [k, missionTime(ms, k)]),
  );
  return {
    earth: { utc: new Date(ms).toISOString(), ...julianDates(ms), taiMinusUtc: taiMinusUtc(ms) },
    mars: { ...t, season: season(t.ls) },
    interimm: i,
    missions,
  };
}
```
